name: Hinduism
support: Chāndogya Upaniṣad 3.17.4 (ahiṃsā among the virtues); Bhagavad Gita 16.2, 13.7, 10.5, 17.14 (ahiṃsā); Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā or other Yajurveda 'mā hiṃsīt' formulas; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa on the sin of killing a person; Mahabharata 'ahiṃsā paramo dharmaḥ' (Tier 2, not counted); Manusmṛti on murder and its penances (Tier 2, contested, not counted).
counter: Atharva Veda abhicāra (rites to kill an enemy), with Śabara on Mīmāṃsā Sūtra 1.1.2 on the śyena rite as harmful and not dharma (a reconciliation); Puruṣamedha in Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 13.6 (victims released?); Śunaḥśepa in Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 7.13 to 18; Ṛg Veda 10.18.7 to 8 and widow-burning (sati) texts in the law books (Tier 2); graded penances by the victim's class (Manusmṛti 11, Tier 2: graded protection); killing an assailant (ātatāyin) in Manusmṛti 8.350 to 351 (defence, so consistent with K1's exception); Bhagavad Gita 2.19 to 38 (war, context only); any text on killing infants, slaves or wives.

name: Judaism
support: Exodus 20:13 (lo tirṣaḥ); Genesis 9:6; Deuteronomy 5:17; Exodus 21:12 to 14; Leviticus 24:17; Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (whoever destroys a single life); Babylonian Talmud Pesachim 25b and Sanhedrin 74a (be killed rather than kill: 'who says your blood is redder'); Exodus 21:20 (a slave killed under the master's hand is avenged).
counter: Numbers 25:6 to 13 and Psalm 106:30 to 31 (Phinehas kills Zimri and Cozbi and is rewarded), with Sanhedrin 81b to 82a (zealots may strike, only during the act; 'the law, but we do not instruct so'); Numbers 35:19 to 27 (the blood avenger may kill a manslayer found outside the city of refuge), with Makkot 12a; Deuteronomy 13:7 to 12 (the enticer; read as judicial); Exodus 21:20 to 21 (slave lingering a day or two); Exodus 22:1 to 2 (thief at night: defence); Deuteronomy 20:16 to 17, 1 Samuel 15:3, Numbers 31:17 (war: context only, but record for K3), with rabbinic limits (peace first, the seven nations no longer identifiable, Mishnah Yadayim 4:4); Judges 11 (Jephthah, narrative); Genesis 22 (Akedah, stopped). Karaite readings.

name: Zoroastrianism
support: Gathas: Yasna 29.1 (lament against fury and violence), 30.6, 32.10 to 14 (those who destroy life?), 48.7, 49.4; Yasna Haptanghaiti; Yasna 12 (Fravarane creed: renounce raiding and harm, but note it names Mazdayasnian villages); Vendidad, Fargard 4 (graded assault, killing?); Pahlavi texts (Tier 2, NOT treated as primary: see corpus.md) on murder as a grave sin.
counter: Yasna 33.2 (one who wrongs the follower of the Lie by word, thought or both hands; Mills on sacred-texts.com, sbe31011.htm), 47.4, 31.18 ('with the weapon'), 46.6, 53.8 to 9 (rulers and evildoers: context); Vendidad passages that call for killing a person for ritual offences or declare a person 'worthy of death' (margarzān), and whether a private person may carry it out; Pahlavi texts on killing heretics (Tier 2, not counted). Branch rule: reformists accept only the Gathas; traditionalists also the Younger Avesta and Vendidad.

name: Buddhism
support: First precept (pāṇātipātā veramaṇī); Dhammapada 129 to 130; Sutta Nipāta 2.14 (Dhammika Sutta: do not kill or cause to kill); Majjhima Nikāya 41; Vinaya, Pārājika 3 (a monk who deliberately kills a human is defeated); Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.177 (trade in weapons and beings); Mahāyāna and Tibetan parallels; Brahmajāla Sūtra major precept 1 (East Asian Mahāyāna).
counter: Mahāyāna Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra on killing icchantikas and the king who killed brahmins who slandered the Mahāyāna (check corpus.md for whether Mahāyāna sutras are treated as primary for Mahāyāna); Upāyakauśalya (Skill in Means) Sūtra, captain who kills a would-be murderer of 500 (fits K1's exception); Mahāvaṃsa 25 (outside the canon); Aṅgulimāla (MN 86, narrative); Jātaka stories with killing; Tibetan 'liberation' rites (outside the corpus).

name: Jainism
support: Ācārāṅga Sūtra I.1 to I.4 (no living being to be killed); Tattvārtha Sūtra 7.1, 7.8 = 7.13 (definition of harm), 7.20 = 7.25; Sūtrakṛtāṅga I.11; Uttarādhyayana; Daśavaikālika 6.
counter: Defence and the householder's partial vow (killing in defence or in a king's duty); stories of Jain kings at war; Kālakācārya story (Tier 2 narrative); any text allowing killing of a person by a householder. Voluntary death (sallekhanā) is exclusion (d).

name: Confucianism
support: Mencius 2A.2 (would not kill one innocent person to gain the empire: 行一不義、殺一不辜而得天下，皆不為也); Mencius 7A.33 (殺一無罪非仁也); Mencius 1A.6 (one who does not delight in killing); Analects 12.19 (why use killing in government); Doctrine of the Mean; Great Learning.
counter: Book of Rites (Tier 2, uncounted) on avenging a father: 父之讎弗與共戴天 (Qu Li I; Tan Gong); Gongyang Zhuan on revenge (Tier 2); Analects 14.34 (repay injury with straightness); Mencius 7B.7 (killing another's father); Mencius 1B.8 (killing a tyrant: ruler context); Mencius 7A.35 (Shun and his father the murderer).

name: Taoism
support: Tao Te Ching 31 (weapons ill-omened; killing many mourned), 30, 67 (compassion), 74 (do not take the executioner's place); Zhuangzi passages on preserving life; Treatise on Response and Retribution (Ganying Pian, Tier 2) listing killing among wicked deeds; Hundred and Eighty Precepts (Tier 2).
counter: Tao Te Ching 5 (straw dogs: image); Zhuangzi stories involving killing; Taoist religious codes allowing killing (unlikely); state punishment texts (context).

name: Stoicism
support: Seneca, Letter 95.30 to 33 ('homo, sacra res homini'; murder and war condemned); De Clementia; De Ira 3.40 (Vedius Pollio and the slave condemned); Epictetus, Discourses (kinship of all people); Marcus Aurelius, Meditations; Musonius Rufus, Lecture 15 (Tier 2, against exposing infants).
counter: Seneca, De Ira 1.15.2 (drowning weak or deformed newborns as an act of reason: 'liberos quoque, si debiles monstrosique editi sunt, mergimus'); Roman paternal power of life and death in De Clementia 1.14 to 1.16; Seneca on tyrannicide; Stoic acceptance of suicide (exclusion (d)); Epictetus 1.23 on raising children (possible reconciliation); Cicero (Tier 2, flagged, not a Stoic).

name: Christianity
support: Exodus 20:13; Genesis 9:6; Matthew 5:21 to 22 and 19:18; Romans 13:9 to 10; 1 John 3:15; Matthew 26:52; Didache 2.2 (Tier 2: do not kill a child, whether before or after birth).
counter: Numbers 25:6 to 13 and Psalm 106:30 to 31 (Phinehas, praised); 1 Kings 18:40 (Elijah and the prophets of Baal); Exodus 21:20 to 21; Numbers 35:19 to 27 (blood avenger); Deuteronomy 13:6 to 10 (enticer); war texts (Deuteronomy 20:16 to 17; 1 Samuel 15:3; Joshua 6:21): context, record for K3; Luke 19:27 (parable); Acts 5 (Ananias, God's act). Christian reconciliations: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae II-II q.64 aa.2 to 3 and 6 (only public authority may kill a malefactor; never lawful to kill the innocent), and on Phinehas (divine instigation); Augustine. Branches: Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant canons differ (Sirach etc.).

name: Islam
support: Qur'an 5:32; 6:151; 17:31; 17:33; 4:29; 4:92 to 93; 25:68; 81:8 to 9 (the buried girl); 60:12; Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6878 (a Muslim's blood is lawful only in three cases: court); 3166 (whoever kills one under covenant, mu'āhad, will not smell Paradise); 3015 (women and children not to be killed in war: K3); Muslim 1498 (Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda: no killing a man found with one's wife; bring witnesses).
counter: Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4361 and 4362 (a blind man kills his slave mother of his children, and a man kills a Jewish woman, for insulting the Prophet; the Prophet declares their blood shed with impunity, hadar: check grading by al-Albānī and whether this counts for Sunni Islam under METHOD.md section 9, decision 5); Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 111 and 6915 ('a Muslim is not killed for a kāfir': graded protection?); Bukhārī 6922 (apostate: ruler context); Qur'an 2:178 to 179 (qiṣāṣ: court context); killing of a slave by a master (Abū Dāwūd 4515 and its grading); Qur'an 9:5 and 47:4 (war: context, K3). Shia sources (Nahj al-Balāgha; al-Kāfī) where possible.

name: Sikhism
support: Guru Granth Sahib: Kabir's saloks against killing living beings (around ang 1350, 1374 to 1375); ang 1384 (Farid: break no heart); ang 140 to 141 (blood-stained garment; another's due); Sikh Rehat Maryada (Tier 2): no killing of daughters (kuṛī-mār).
counter: Defence and just war: Zafarnama (Dasam Granth, contested, not counted): when all means fail it is right to draw the sword (defence or war: context); any Guru Granth Sahib passage approving a killing. Rehat Maryada bans on association with killers of daughters.

name: Bahá'í Faith
support: Kitáb-i-Aqdas ¶19 (murder forbidden; VERIFIED lead: bahai-library.com/writings/bahaullah/aqdas/aqdas2/K19.htm) and ¶73; Gleanings; Kitáb-i-Aqdas on abolition of holy war (Lawḥ-i-Bishárát; Tablet of Glad-Tidings); Hidden Words; 'Abdu'l-Bahá (treated as primary).
counter: Kitáb-i-Aqdas ¶62 (murder and arson: death or life imprisonment, a court matter: context); any text permitting private killing; Bábí-era laws (the Báb's Bayán, which the Aqdas supersedes).

name: Secular humanism
support: Amsterdam Declaration 2022 ('helping and not harming'; human rights); Humanist Manifesto III; Amsterdam Declarations 1952 and 2002; A Secular Humanist Declaration (1980); Humanist Manifesto II (1973); IHEU Minimum Statement (1996).
counter: Positions on euthanasia and abortion (exclusions (c) and (d): context only); any declaration text that accepts killing a person on private authority (unlikely); limits of 'not harming' as aspiration rather than rule.
